# AI Review Protocol

This file is the durable coordination contract between Eric, Codex, Claude CLI, and any Codex subagents working on this Diablo II Resurrected mod repository.

If a conversation restarts, read this file before starting risky design or code/data work.

## Current Review Mechanism

As of 2026-05-21, Claude review is performed by direct Claude CLI invocation from Codex. Do not rely on a separate Claude desktop/app session as the normal workflow.

Claude CLI is available as:

```text
C:\Users\ericb\.local\bin\claude.exe
```

The initialized reviewer session is:

```text
name: d2r-codex-reviewer
session_id: da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e
model: opus
observed_model: claude-opus-4-7
```

Use the `opus` model alias so the CLI selects the latest Opus model available to the account. Resume the existing session when practical, but do not assume Claude has complete prior conversation memory. Every review prompt must include the original user request, current git status, relevant durable docs, and the exact diff or design being reviewed.

Recommended code-review invocation pattern:

```powershell
claude --model opus --name d2r-codex-reviewer --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep -p "<review prompt>" --output-format json
```

If resuming the existing reviewer session, use:

```powershell
claude --resume da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e --model opus --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep -p "<review prompt>" --output-format json
```

If resume fails or the session is not available, start a fresh CLI review and pass full context in the prompt.

Claude CLI is a read-only reviewer. Do not give Claude edit/write/publish tools for normal reviews. Codex implements changes, then re-runs Claude CLI until consensus is reached.

CLI consensus is reached only when:

- Claude CLI's latest verdict is `APPROVED` or `approved_with_notes`.
- Claude reports zero Critical findings.
- Claude reports zero High findings.
- Codex has implemented every required fix or has explicitly documented why a remaining finding is intentionally rejected.
- Codex has re-run Claude after required fixes when Claude requested changes.

Before committing, Codex should record the last Claude verdict and session/run id in its final work notes or commit summary.

The older `docs\ai-review\tasks\...` queue format may still be useful for archived design records, but it is no longer the primary mechanism for new reviews unless Eric explicitly asks to use the file queue.

## Paths

Primary repository:

```text
C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh
```

Main working branch:

```text
xav-custom
```

Live game folder:

```text
E:\Diablo II Resurrected\mods\XavReimagined\XavReimagined.mpq
```

Launch arguments:

```text
-mod XavReimagined -txt
```

Legacy review queue root:

```text
C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh\docs\ai-review
```

Task folders:

```text
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\
```

## Purpose

Codex is the primary implementer. Claude CLI is an independent reviewer. The review loop exists to catch design mistakes, data-table risks, tooltip/gameplay mismatches, unsafe TSV edits, and cases where a change technically modifies files but misses Eric's gameplay intent.

For small obvious edits, Codex may skip Claude review. For skill changes, missile changes, cube recipes, itemization passes, treasure classes, TSV-wide changes, live-publish-sensitive work, or anything with tooltip/gameplay mismatch risk, run direct Claude CLI review before committing.

## Roles

Eric:

- Provides gameplay/design requests.
- Can override the review loop.
- Decides ambiguous product/design tradeoffs.

Codex:

- Writes designs, patches, code, data changes, docs, commits, pushes, and live publishes when appropriate.
- Runs direct Claude CLI review before committing risky work.
- Includes Eric's original request verbatim in every review prompt.
- Includes current git status, relevant docs, and the exact diff or design in every review prompt.
- Reads Claude reviews, writes Codex responses, and either fixes issues or explains why findings are rejected.
- Marks consensus reached.

Claude CLI:

- Reviews only.
- Does not edit gameplay/data/code files.
- Does not publish to the live game folder.
- Does not commit or push.
- Returns structured review findings to Codex.

Codex subagents:

- Follow this same protocol when assigned design/code/data work that needs review.
- Do not bypass Claude for risky work.
- Do not publish, push, or touch the live game folder unless the parent Codex agent explicitly assigns that responsibility.

## Folder Layout

Legacy queue tasks live in their own folder:

```text
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\
  request.md
  design.md              optional
  diff.patch             optional
  claude-review-r01.md   written by Claude
  codex-response-r01.md  written by Codex
  claude-review-r02.md   later rounds as needed
  codex-response-r02.md
  claude.lock            temporary lock file
```

Completed or obsolete tasks may be moved to:

```text
docs\ai-review\archive\
```

```text
draft
ready_for_claude
claude_in_progress
claude_reviewed
codex_in_progress
consensus_reached
blocked_needs_user
cancelled
```

Normal code review loop:

```text
ready_for_claude
claude_in_progress
claude_reviewed
codex_in_progress
ready_for_claude
...
consensus_reached
```

Claude never marks a task `consensus_reached`. Codex does that after reading Claude's latest review and writing a Codex response.

## Consensus

Consensus is reached when:

- Claude's latest verdict is `approved` or `approved_with_notes`.
- There are zero Critical findings.
- There are zero High findings.
- Codex has either implemented or explicitly rejected remaining findings in `codex-response-rXX.md`.

If `max_rounds` is reached and serious issues remain, Codex should mark the task `blocked_needs_user` and ask Eric to decide.

```yaml
---
schema: ai-review-task-v1
id: 2026-05-14-example-task
status: ready_for_claude
phase: design_review
round: 1
max_rounds: 3
created_by: codex
created_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
updated_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
repo: C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh
branch: xav-custom
base_ref: HEAD
head_ref:
original_user_request_included: true
live_publish_allowed: false
last_review:
last_verdict:
claimed_by:
claimed_at:
reviewed_at:
---
```

Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC:

```text
2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
```

Every `request.md` must include Eric's original request exactly:

````markdown
## Original User Request

```text
<Eric's original request copied verbatim>
```
````

Claude validates both the flag and this section. If the section is missing or empty, Claude marks the task `blocked_needs_user`.

## Request Body Template

Use this body shape:

````markdown
# Review Request

## Original User Request

```text
<Eric's original request copied verbatim>
```

## Goal

Short description of what Codex is trying to accomplish.

## Phase

design_review | code_review | re_review

## Scope

- Files expected to change
- Systems affected
- Known constraints

## Design Or Diff

Point to `design.md`, `diff.patch`, commits, or both.

## Review Questions

1. Does this match Eric's request?
2. What are the likely D2R modding risks?
3. Are active/base files synchronized where needed?
4. Are TSV structures safe?
5. Are tooltip and gameplay values likely consistent?
6. Is this safe to publish/playtest?
````

## Claude Lock File

Claude uses `claude.lock` to avoid duplicate automated reviews.

Lock content:

```yaml
schema: ai-review-lock-v1
task_id: <task-id>
reviewer: claude
reviewer_model:
created_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
```

Lock rules:

- If `claude.lock` is less than 2 hours old, Claude skips the task.
- If `claude.lock` is 2 hours old or older, Claude may replace it and note that in the review.
- Claude removes the lock after writing its review and updating `request.md`.

## Claude Startup Behavior

Claude should:

1. Scan `docs\ai-review\tasks\*\request.md`.
2. Find the oldest task with `status: ready_for_claude`.
3. Sort by `created_at`, then `id`, then file mtime as fallback.
4. Process one task at a time.
5. If no task is ready, say exactly:

```text
No pending review requests.
```

Missing queue root is treated as an empty queue.

## Claude Allowed Writes

Claude may write only:

```text
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\claude-review-rXX.md
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\request.md frontmatter status fields only
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\claude.lock
```

Claude must not write:

```text
data\
scripts\
E:\Diablo II Resurrected\
git branches or refs
source/game/mod files outside docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>
```

## Claude Review Format

Claude writes `claude-review-rXX.md`, where `XX` is the current round.

Frontmatter:

```yaml
---
schema: ai-review-result-v1
task_id: <task-id>
round: 1
reviewer: claude
verdict: needs_fixes
critical: 0
high: 1
medium: 2
low: 0
requires_codex_changes: true
```

```text

approved_with_notes
needs_fixes
high_risk_do_not_publish
blocked_needs_info
```

```markdown
## Summary

## Findings

Group by Critical, High, Medium, Low.

Each finding includes:

## Codex Action Items

## Suggested Follow-up Tests
```

40	```

52	- Claude reports zero High findings.

98	## Purpose
99	
100	Codex is the primary implementer. Claude CLI is an independent reviewer. The review loop exists to catch design mistakes, data-table risks, tooltip/gameplay mismatches, unsafe TSV edits, and cases where a change technically modifies files but misses Eric's gameplay intent.
101	
102	For small obvious edits, Codex may skip Claude review. For skill changes, missile changes, cube recipes, itemization passes, treasure classes, TSV-wide changes, live-publish-sensitive work, or anything with tooltip/gameplay mismatch risk, run direct Claude CLI review before committing.
103

# Claude Review

## Verdict

APPROVED — with two Medium notes worth fixing before this becomes load-bearing.

## Summary

Codex implemented a wrapper-based persistent review history that meets Eric's intent: every Codex-triggered Claude review now runs through `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1`, which writes the prompt, raw JSON, rendered review, metadata, mirrored session jsonl, and mirrored project memory under `docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/`. Native Claude Code sessions correctly remain local — only the per-run mirror is repo-side. The wrapper enforces read-only review via `--tools Read,Glob,Grep` and `--permission-mode dontAsk`, and it does **not** copy credentials, cache directories, or telemetry. The slug computed by `Get-ClaudeProjectSlug` (`C--Dropbox-AI-projects-d2r-d2r-reimagined-fresh`) matches the real `.claude/projects/` directory layout, which I can confirm from my own memory dir path. AGENTS.md and protocol.md both correctly steer to the wrapper as the canonical entry point and demote the raw `claude` invocation to a debugging fallback.

## Findings

### High

None.

### Medium

- **MEDIUM-001 — `2>&1` merge can break JSON parse on a "success" run**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` line 70
  - Issue: `& claude @claudeArgs 2>&1` captures stderr into the same stream as stdout. If `claude` emits any non-fatal stderr line on a successful run (deprecation warnings, auto-update notices, transient network warnings, etc.), `$raw` will contain non-JSON noise mixed with the JSON. `result.json` still gets written (good), but `ConvertFrom-Json` on line 79 will throw, no `review.md` is produced, and the caller sees a parse error rather than a clean review. Exit code 0 + parse failure currently masquerades as a script bug rather than a CLI warning.
  - Why it matters: Once this is the canonical pre-commit gate, a single one-off stderr line silently blocks reviews in a confusing way.
  - Suggested fix: Either (a) capture stderr separately, e.g. `& claude @claudeArgs 2> (Join-Path $runDir 'stderr.log')`, and only parse stdout; or (b) keep the merge but try the JSON parse defensively and, on failure, extract the largest balanced `{...}` substring before giving up.
  - Blocks approval: no (per the protocol's CLI consensus rule only Critical/High block)

- **MEDIUM-002 — Mirrored session.jsonl and memory/*.md may contain sensitive prior-conversation content that will land in git**
  - Files: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` lines 89–102; `docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/README.md`
  - Issue: `<session-id>.jsonl` is the full Claude Code conversation transcript including every tool input/output the assistant saw in that session — file contents read, paths inspected, prompts containing diffs, etc. Mirroring it into the repo is intentional per Eric's request, but the README and protocol.md don't warn that this snapshot becomes a permanent, publicly-committable artifact. Same applies to `memory/*.md`, which today contains user profile, feedback, and project memories. None of *my* current memory files contain secrets, but a future memory write of "API token = …" or a future review that reads a `.env` file into a tool result would silently propagate to the repo and any GitHub push.
  - Why it matters: Eric asked for persistence; he hasn't necessarily signed off on indiscriminate inclusion of any sensitive content that ever appears in Claude's local state. A warning in the README plus a pre-commit reminder in protocol.md is cheap insurance.
  - Suggested fix: Add to `docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/README.md`: "Session transcripts and memory mirrors are committed to the repo. Before pushing, sanity-check the latest run's `session.jsonl` and `memory/*.md` for content you do not want in version control (tokens, private file contents, etc.). The wrapper deliberately does not auto-redact." Optional: also add a `-NoMirror` switch to the wrapper for one-off sensitive reviews.
  - Blocks approval: no

### Low

- **LOW-001 — Very large prompts may hit Windows process-arg length limit**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` line 66
  - Issue: `-p $promptText` passes the entire prompt as a single command-line argument. Diff-heavy reviews can easily push past Windows' practical process-argument ceiling (~32K chars). The wrapper currently doesn't have a fallback to stdin.
  - Suggested fix: If `claude` accepts a prompt via stdin (e.g., `claude … -p -` or piped input), gate on `$promptText.Length` and switch to stdin past ~30000 chars. Optional, can be deferred until it bites.
  - Blocks approval: no

- **LOW-002 — Sub-second timestamp collisions**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` lines 43–45
  - Issue: `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ` has second-level resolution. Two reviews fired in the same second produce the same `runDir` and the second `New-Item -Force` quietly reuses the first. Realistically only an issue if someone scripts a fan-out.
  - Suggested fix: Append `-{0:D4} -f (Get-Random -Maximum 10000)` or the process ID.
  - Blocks approval: no

- **LOW-003 — Memory mirror keeps only the latest snapshot**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` lines 97–102
  - Issue: Each run overwrites `docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/memory/*.md`. The `runs/<timestamp>/` dir captures `session.jsonl` per run, but not memory. Future "what did Claude know at the time of review X" investigations will be lossy.
  - Suggested fix: Also copy memory snapshot under `runs/<timestamp>/memory/` (cheap, small files).
  - Blocks approval: no

- **LOW-004 — Memory copy is non-recursive**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` line 99
  - Issue: `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $localMemoryDir -File -Filter '*.md'` only sees top-level `*.md`. My memory dir is currently flat, so this works today, but if memories are ever organized into subfolders the mirror silently drops them.
  - Suggested fix: Add `-Recurse` and preserve subdir structure with a small `Resolve-Path` walk; or document the flat-only assumption.
  - Blocks approval: no

- **LOW-005 — No `claude` PATH check / no fallback to documented absolute path**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` line 70
  - Issue: Script calls `& claude` directly. Protocol.md documents `C:\Users\ericb\.local\bin\claude.exe` as the canonical location. If a future Codex shell loses PATH, the script errors out generically.
  - Suggested fix: Add a `[string]$ClaudeExe = 'claude'` parameter and `& $ClaudeExe @claudeArgs`, with a `Get-Command` probe up front that falls back to the documented path.
  - Blocks approval: no

- **LOW-006 — No guard / metadata field when `result.result` is missing**
  - File: `scripts/invoke-claude-review.ps1` lines 80–82
  - Issue: If Claude returns a JSON envelope with no `.result` (unusual but possible — e.g., a thinking-only response or future format change), no `review.md` is written and `metadata.json.verdict_recorded_by_claude` stays `$null` with no other signal. Caller relying on `ReviewPath` will get a path that doesn't exist.
  - Suggested fix: Write a stub `review.md` ("No `.result` field in CLI output — see result.json") and set a `result_present = $false` flag in metadata.
  - Blocks approval: no

- **LOW-007 — Wording: "latest mirrored session transcript"**
  - File: `docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/README.md` line 18
  - Issue: The README phrasing implies only one file lives in `sessions/`, but the wrapper writes one jsonl per distinct session id. Over time `sessions/` will accumulate multiple files.
  - Suggested fix: Rephrase to "mirrored session transcript per session id". Trivially small.
  - Blocks approval: no

## Validation Checks

- Original user request reviewed: yes
- Git diff or design reviewed: working-tree state of all four in-scope files reviewed; supplied diff was again truncated at `-p <review`, but the live files are intact
- TSV column counts checked: n/a (no TSV touched)
- Active/base sync checked: n/a
- Tooltip vs gameplay consistency considered: n/a
- Live publish risk considered: yes — script does not touch live folder; protocol publish rule unchanged
- Docs checked: yes (AGENTS.md, protocol.md, claude-cli-history/README.md)
- Read-only review constraint preserved: yes — `--tools Read,Glob,Grep` + `--permission-mode dontAsk` and confirmed against this session's tool surface
- Credentials/cache/telemetry exclusion: yes — only `<session-id>.jsonl` and `memory/*.md` are copied; no `.credentials*`, no cache dirs, no statsig
- Claude project slug correctness: yes — `Get-ClaudeProjectSlug` output matches the real `C--Dropbox-AI-projects-d2r-d2r-reimagined-fresh` directory

## Codex Action Items

1. (Recommended before this becomes load-bearing) MEDIUM-001: split stderr from stdout in the wrapper so a stray warning doesn't break the JSON parse.
2. (Recommended) MEDIUM-002: add a one-paragraph "what's in here / what to sanity-check before pushing" warning to `docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/README.md` and a one-line nudge in protocol.md near the existing "make sure history files are included in version control" sentence.
3. Optional cleanup: any of LOW-001 through LOW-007 as you encounter the corresponding pain.
4. Record this verdict (APPROVED, MEDIUM notes left intentional) and the reviewer session id in the commit summary, per the existing protocol rule at protocol.md line 68.

## Suggested Follow-up Tests

- Run the wrapper end-to-end against a synthetic small prompt and verify all of: `runs/<ts>/prompt.md`, `runs/<ts>/result.json`, `runs/<ts>/review.md`, `runs/<ts>/metadata.json`, `runs/<ts>/session.jsonl`, `sessions/<session-id>.jsonl`, `memory/*.md`, and `latest-run.json` exist and contain expected content.
- Force a non-zero exit (e.g., bad model name) and confirm `result.json` is still saved and the wrapper throws with a clear message.
- Force a non-JSON stderr line on a success path (run with a flag the CLI deprecates) to confirm/demonstrate MEDIUM-001 in practice.
- After commit, `git log -- docs/ai-review/claude-cli-history/` to verify history is actually tracked and not gitignored anywhere upstream.

Verdict: **APPROVED** — zero Critical, zero High. Codex is clear to commit. Strongly suggest folding in MEDIUM-001 and MEDIUM-002 in a follow-up; both are quick changes and meaningfully harden the new mechanism.

1	# AI Review Protocol
2	
3	This file is the durable coordination contract between Eric, Codex, Claude CLI, and any Codex subagents working on this Diablo II Resurrected mod repository.
4	
5	If a conversation restarts, read this file before starting risky design or code/data work.
6	
7	## Current Review Mechanism
8	
9	As of 2026-05-21, Claude review is performed by direct Claude CLI invocation from Codex. Do not rely on a separate Claude desktop/app session as the normal workflow.
10	
11	Claude CLI is available as:
12	
13	```text
14	C:\Users\ericb\.local\bin\claude.exe
15	```
16	
17	The initialized reviewer session is:
18	
19	```text
20	name: d2r-codex-reviewer
21	session_id: da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e
22	model: opus
23	observed_model: claude-opus-4-7
24	```
25	
26	Use the `opus` model alias so the CLI selects the latest Opus model available to the account. Resume the existing session when practical, but do not assume Claude has complete prior conversation memory. Every review prompt must include the original user request, current git status, relevant durable docs, and the exact diff or design being reviewed.
27	
28	Recommended code-review invocation pattern:
29	
30	```powershell
31	powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\invoke-claude-review.ps1 -PromptPath <prompt.md> -ReviewName <short-name>
32	```
33	
34	The wrapper stores prompts, raw results, rendered reviews, metadata, mirrored session transcripts, and mirrored Claude project memory under:
35	
36	```text
37	docs\ai-review\claude-cli-history\
38	```
39	
40	Use the raw `claude` command only when debugging the wrapper. The canonical raw command is:
41	
42	```powershell
43	claude --model opus --name d2r-codex-reviewer --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep -p "<review prompt>" --output-format json
44	```
45	
46	These flags were verified against `claude --help` for Claude Code 2.1.146 and the command was successfully run from Codex on 2026-05-21.
47	
48	If resuming the existing reviewer session, use:
49	
50	```powershell
51	claude --resume da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e --model opus --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep -p "<review prompt>" --output-format json
52	```
53	
54	If resume fails or the session is not available, start a fresh CLI review and pass full context in the prompt.
55	
56	For multi-line prompts, build the prompt as a PowerShell here-string and pass it with `-p $prompt`; do not paste a large diff directly inside quoted command text.
57	
58	Claude CLI is a read-only reviewer. Do not give Claude edit/write/publish tools for normal reviews. Codex implements changes, then re-runs Claude CLI until consensus is reached.
59	
60	CLI consensus is reached only when:
61	
62	- Claude CLI's latest verdict is `APPROVED` or `approved_with_notes`.
63	- Claude reports zero Critical findings.
64	- Claude reports zero High findings.
65	- Codex has implemented every required fix or has explicitly documented why a remaining finding is intentionally rejected.
66	- Codex has re-run Claude after required fixes when Claude requested changes.
67	
68	Before committing, Codex should record the last Claude verdict and session/run id in its final work notes or commit summary.
69	
70	Before committing, Codex should also make sure the relevant `docs\ai-review\claude-cli-history\...` files for the review are included in version control unless Eric explicitly asks not to store that review history. Sanity-check the mirrored `session.jsonl` and `memory\*.md` files before pushing because they preserve review context exactly and are not auto-redacted.
71	
72	The older `docs\ai-review\tasks\...` queue format may still be useful for archived design records, but it is no longer the primary mechanism for new reviews unless Eric explicitly asks to use the file queue.
73	
74	## Paths
75	
76	Primary repository:
77	
78	```text
79	C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh
80	```
81	
82	Main working branch:
83	
84	```text
85	xav-custom
86	```
87	
88	Live game folder:
89	
90	```text
91	E:\Diablo II Resurrected\mods\XavReimagined\XavReimagined.mpq
92	```
93	
94	Launch arguments:
95	
96	```text
97	-mod XavReimagined -txt
98	```
99	
100	Legacy review queue root:
101	
102	```text
103	C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh\docs\ai-review
104	```
105	
106	Task folders:
107	
108	```text
109	docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\
110	```
111	
112	## Purpose
113	
114	Codex is the primary implementer. Claude CLI is an independent reviewer. The review loop exists to catch design mistakes, data-table risks, tooltip/gameplay mismatches, unsafe TSV edits, and cases where a change technically modifies files but misses Eric's gameplay intent.
115	
116	For small obvious edits, Codex may skip Claude review. For skill changes, missile changes, cube recipes, itemization passes, treasure classes, TSV-wide changes, live-publish-sensitive work, or anything with tooltip/gameplay mismatch risk, run direct Claude CLI review before committing.
117	
118	## Roles
119	
120	Eric:
121	
122	- Provides gameplay/design requests.
123	- Can override the review loop.
124	- Decides ambiguous product/design tradeoffs.
125	
126	Codex:
127	
128	- Writes designs, patches, code, data changes, docs, commits, pushes, and live publishes when appropriate.
129	- Runs direct Claude CLI review before committing risky work.
130	- Includes Eric's original request verbatim in every review prompt.
131	- Includes current git status, relevant docs, and the exact diff or design in every review prompt.
132	- Reads Claude reviews, writes Codex responses, and either fixes issues or explains why findings are rejected.
133	- Marks consensus reached.
134	
135	Claude CLI:
136	
137	- Reviews only.
138	- Does not edit gameplay/data/code files.
139	- Does not publish to the live game folder.
140	- Does not commit or push.
141	- Returns structured review findings to Codex.
142	
143	Codex subagents:
144	
145	- Follow this same protocol when assigned design/code/data work that needs review.
146	- Do not bypass Claude for risky work.
147	- Do not publish, push, or touch the live game folder unless the parent Codex agent explicitly assigns that responsibility.
148	
149	## Legacy Review Queue
150	
151	The sections below describe the older file-queue mechanism. Do not use them for new reviews unless Eric explicitly asks to use the queue.
152	
153	### Folder Layout
154	
155	Legacy queue tasks live in their own folder:
156	
157	```text
158	docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\
159	  request.md
160	  design.md              optional
161	  diff.patch             optional
162	  claude-review-r01.md   written by Claude
163	  codex-response-r01.md  written by Codex
164	  claude-review-r02.md   later rounds as needed
165	  codex-response-r02.md
166	  claude.lock            temporary lock file
167	```
168	
169	Completed or obsolete tasks may be moved to:
170	
171	```text
172	docs\ai-review\archive\
173	```
174	
175	### Task Statuses
176	
177	Use these `request.md` frontmatter statuses:
178	
179	```text
180	draft
181	ready_for_claude
182	claude_in_progress
183	claude_reviewed
184	codex_in_progress
185	consensus_reached
186	blocked_needs_user
187	cancelled
188	```
189	
190	Normal code review loop:
191	
192	```text
193	ready_for_claude
194	claude_in_progress
195	claude_reviewed
196	codex_in_progress
197	ready_for_claude
198	...
199	consensus_reached
200	```
201	
202	Claude never marks a task `consensus_reached`. Codex does that after reading Claude's latest review and writing a Codex response.
203	
204	### Legacy Queue Consensus
205	
206	Legacy queue consensus is reached when:
207	
208	- Claude's latest verdict is `approved` or `approved_with_notes`.
209	- There are zero Critical findings.
210	- There are zero High findings.
211	- Codex has either implemented or explicitly rejected remaining findings in `codex-response-rXX.md`.
212	
213	If `max_rounds` is reached and serious issues remain, Codex should mark the task `blocked_needs_user` and ask Eric to decide.
214	
215	### Request File Format
216	
217	`request.md` must include YAML frontmatter:
218	
219	```yaml
220	---
221	schema: ai-review-task-v1
222	id: 2026-05-14-example-task
223	status: ready_for_claude
224	phase: design_review
225	round: 1
226	max_rounds: 3
227	created_by: codex
228	created_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
229	updated_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
230	repo: C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh
231	branch: xav-custom

233	head_ref:
234	original_user_request_included: true
235	live_publish_allowed: false
236	last_review:
237	last_verdict:
238	claimed_by:
239	claimed_at:
240	reviewed_at:
241	---
242	```
243	
244	Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC:
245	
246	```text
247	2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
248	```
249	
250	Every `request.md` must include Eric's original request exactly:
251	
252	````markdown
253	## Original User Request
254	
255	```text
256	<Eric's original request copied verbatim>
257	```
258	````
259	
260	Claude validates both the flag and this section. If the section is missing or empty, Claude marks the task `blocked_needs_user`.
261	
262	### Request Body Template
263	
264	Use this body shape:
265	
266	````markdown
267	# Review Request
268	
269	## Original User Request
270	
271	```text
272	<Eric's original request copied verbatim>
273	```
274	
275	## Goal
276	
277	Short description of what Codex is trying to accomplish.

279	## Phase
280	
281	design_review | code_review | re_review
282	
283	## Scope
284	
285	- Files expected to change
286	- Systems affected
287	- Known constraints
288

291	Point to `design.md`, `diff.patch`, commits, or both.
292	
293	## Review Questions
294	
295	1. Does this match Eric's request?
296	2. What are the likely D2R modding risks?
297	3. Are active/base files synchronized where needed?
298	4. Are TSV structures safe?

301	````

304

312	reviewer: claude

# AI Review Protocol

This file is the durable coordination contract between Eric, Codex, Claude CLI, and any Codex subagents working on this Diablo II Resurrected mod repository.

If a conversation restarts, read this file before starting risky design or code/data work.

## Current Review Mechanism

As of 2026-05-21, Claude review is performed by direct Claude CLI invocation from Codex. Do not rely on a separate Claude desktop/app session as the normal workflow.

Claude CLI is available as:

```text
C:\Users\ericb\.local\bin\claude.exe
```

The initialized reviewer session is:

```text
name: d2r-codex-reviewer
session_id: da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e
model: opus
observed_model: claude-opus-4-7
```

Use the `opus` model alias so the CLI selects the latest Opus model available to the account. Resume the existing session when practical, but do not assume Claude has complete prior conversation memory. Every review prompt must include the original user request, current git status, relevant durable docs, and the exact diff or design being reviewed.

Recommended code-review invocation pattern:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\invoke-claude-review.ps1 -PromptPath <prompt.md> -ReviewName <short-name>
```

The wrapper stores prompts, raw results, rendered reviews, metadata, mirrored session transcripts, and mirrored Claude project memory under:

```text
docs\ai-review\claude-cli-history\
```

Use the raw `claude` command only when debugging the wrapper. The canonical raw command is:

```powershell
claude --model opus --name d2r-codex-reviewer --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep -p "<review prompt>" --output-format json
```

These flags were verified against `claude --help` for Claude Code 2.1.146 and the command was successfully run from Codex on 2026-05-21.

If resuming the existing reviewer session, use:

```powershell
claude --resume da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e --model opus --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read,Glob,Grep -p "<review prompt>" --output-format json
```

If resume fails or the session is not available, start a fresh CLI review and pass full context in the prompt.

For multi-line prompts, build the prompt as a PowerShell here-string and pass it with `-p $prompt`; do not paste a large diff directly inside quoted command text.

Claude CLI is a read-only reviewer. Do not give Claude edit/write/publish tools for normal reviews. Codex implements changes, then re-runs Claude CLI until consensus is reached.

CLI consensus is reached only when:

- Claude CLI's latest verdict is `APPROVED` or `approved_with_notes`.
- Claude reports zero Critical findings.
- Claude reports zero High findings.
- Codex has implemented every required fix or has explicitly documented why a remaining finding is intentionally rejected.
- Codex has re-run Claude after required fixes when Claude requested changes.

Before committing, Codex should record the last Claude verdict and session/run id in its final work notes or commit summary.

Before committing, Codex should also make sure the relevant `docs\ai-review\claude-cli-history\...` files for the review are included in version control unless Eric explicitly asks not to store that review history. Sanity-check the mirrored `session.jsonl` and `memory\*.md` files before pushing because they preserve review context exactly and are not auto-redacted.

The older `docs\ai-review\tasks\...` queue format may still be useful for archived design records, but it is no longer the primary mechanism for new reviews unless Eric explicitly asks to use the file queue.

## Paths

Primary repository:

```text
C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh
```

Main working branch:

```text
xav-custom
```

Live game folder:

```text
E:\Diablo II Resurrected\mods\XavReimagined\XavReimagined.mpq
```

Launch arguments:

```text
-mod XavReimagined -txt
```

Legacy review queue root:

```text
C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh\docs\ai-review
```

Task folders:

```text
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\
```

## Purpose

Codex is the primary implementer. Claude CLI is an independent reviewer. The review loop exists to catch design mistakes, data-table risks, tooltip/gameplay mismatches, unsafe TSV edits, and cases where a change technically modifies files but misses Eric's gameplay intent.

For small obvious edits, Codex may skip Claude review. For skill changes, missile changes, cube recipes, itemization passes, treasure classes, TSV-wide changes, live-publish-sensitive work, or anything with tooltip/gameplay mismatch risk, run direct Claude CLI review before committing.

## Roles

Eric:

- Provides gameplay/design requests.
- Can override the review loop.
- Decides ambiguous product/design tradeoffs.

Codex:

- Writes designs, patches, code, data changes, docs, commits, pushes, and live publishes when appropriate.
- Runs direct Claude CLI review before committing risky work.
- Includes Eric's original request verbatim in every review prompt.
- Includes current git status, relevant docs, and the exact diff or design in every review prompt.
- Reads Claude reviews, writes Codex responses, and either fixes issues or explains why findings are rejected.
- Marks consensus reached.

Claude CLI:

- Reviews only.
- Does not edit gameplay/data/code files.
- Does not publish to the live game folder.
- Does not commit or push.
- Returns structured review findings to Codex.

Codex subagents:

- Follow this same protocol when assigned design/code/data work that needs review.
- Do not bypass Claude for risky work.
- Do not publish, push, or touch the live game folder unless the parent Codex agent explicitly assigns that responsibility.

## Legacy Review Queue

The sections below describe the older file-queue mechanism. Do not use them for new reviews unless Eric explicitly asks to use the queue.

### Folder Layout

Legacy queue tasks live in their own folder:

```text
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\
  request.md
  design.md              optional
  diff.patch             optional
  claude-review-r01.md   written by Claude
  codex-response-r01.md  written by Codex
  claude-review-r02.md   later rounds as needed
  codex-response-r02.md
  claude.lock            temporary lock file
```

Completed or obsolete tasks may be moved to:

```text
docs\ai-review\archive\
```

### Task Statuses

Use these `request.md` frontmatter statuses:

```text
draft
ready_for_claude
claude_in_progress
claude_reviewed
codex_in_progress
consensus_reached
blocked_needs_user
cancelled
```

Normal code review loop:

```text
ready_for_claude
claude_in_progress
claude_reviewed
codex_in_progress
ready_for_claude
...
consensus_reached
```

Claude never marks a task `consensus_reached`. Codex does that after reading Claude's latest review and writing a Codex response.

### Legacy Queue Consensus

Legacy queue consensus is reached when:

- Claude's latest verdict is `approved` or `approved_with_notes`.
- There are zero Critical findings.
- There are zero High findings.
- Codex has either implemented or explicitly rejected remaining findings in `codex-response-rXX.md`.

If `max_rounds` is reached and serious issues remain, Codex should mark the task `blocked_needs_user` and ask Eric to decide.

### Request File Format

`request.md` must include YAML frontmatter:

```yaml
---
schema: ai-review-task-v1
id: 2026-05-14-example-task
status: ready_for_claude
phase: design_review
round: 1
max_rounds: 3
created_by: codex
created_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
updated_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
repo: C:\Dropbox\AI projects\d2r\d2r-reimagined-fresh
branch: xav-custom
base_ref: HEAD
head_ref:
original_user_request_included: true
live_publish_allowed: false
last_review:
last_verdict:
claimed_by:
claimed_at:
reviewed_at:
---
```

Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC:

```text
2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
```

Every `request.md` must include Eric's original request exactly:

````markdown
## Original User Request

```text
<Eric's original request copied verbatim>
```
````

Claude validates both the flag and this section. If the section is missing or empty, Claude marks the task `blocked_needs_user`.

### Request Body Template

Use this body shape:

````markdown
# Review Request

## Original User Request

```text
<Eric's original request copied verbatim>
```

## Goal

Short description of what Codex is trying to accomplish.

## Phase

design_review | code_review | re_review

## Scope

- Files expected to change
- Systems affected
- Known constraints

## Design Or Diff

Point to `design.md`, `diff.patch`, commits, or both.

## Review Questions

1. Does this match Eric's request?
2. What are the likely D2R modding risks?
3. Are active/base files synchronized where needed?
4. Are TSV structures safe?
5. Are tooltip and gameplay values likely consistent?
6. Is this safe to publish/playtest?
````

### Claude Lock File

Claude uses `claude.lock` to avoid duplicate automated reviews.

Lock content:

```yaml
schema: ai-review-lock-v1
task_id: <task-id>
reviewer: claude
reviewer_model:
created_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
```

Lock rules:

- If `claude.lock` is less than 2 hours old, Claude skips the task.
- If `claude.lock` is 2 hours old or older, Claude may replace it and note that in the review.
- Claude removes the lock after writing its review and updating `request.md`.

### Claude Startup Behavior

Claude should:

1. Scan `docs\ai-review\tasks\*\request.md`.
2. Find the oldest task with `status: ready_for_claude`.
3. Sort by `created_at`, then `id`, then file mtime as fallback.
4. Process one task at a time.
5. If no task is ready, say exactly:

```text
No pending review requests.
```

Missing queue root is treated as an empty queue.

### Claude Allowed Writes

Claude may write only:

```text
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\claude-review-rXX.md
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\request.md frontmatter status fields only
docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>\claude.lock
```

Claude must not write:

```text
data\
scripts\
E:\Diablo II Resurrected\
git branches or refs
source/game/mod files outside docs\ai-review\tasks\<task-id>
```

### Claude Review Format

Claude writes `claude-review-rXX.md`, where `XX` is the current round.

Frontmatter:

```yaml
---
schema: ai-review-result-v1
task_id: <task-id>
round: 1
reviewer: claude
verdict: needs_fixes
critical: 0
high: 1
medium: 2
low: 0
requires_codex_changes: true
---
```

Verdicts:

```text
approved
approved_with_notes
needs_fixes
high_risk_do_not_publish
blocked_needs_info
```

Body:

```markdown
# Claude Review

## Verdict

Approved | Approved with notes | Needs fixes | High risk / do not publish | Blocked / needs info

## Summary

Briefly summarize what Codex proposed or changed, and whether it matches Eric's original request.

## Findings

Group by Critical, High, Medium, Low.

Each finding includes:

- ID, such as HIGH-001
- File path
- Row/item/skill/line if applicable
- Issue
- Why it matters
- Suggested fix
- Whether it blocks approval

## Validation Checks

Say yes/no for:

- Original user request reviewed
- Git diff or design reviewed
- TSV column counts checked
- Active/base sync checked
- Tooltip vs gameplay consistency considered
- Live publish risk considered
- Docs checked

## Codex Action Items

Exact actions for Codex.

## Suggested Follow-up Tests

Practical script or in-game tests.
```

### Codex Response Format

Codex writes `codex-response-rXX.md` after reading Claude's review.

Frontmatter:

```yaml
---
schema: ai-review-response-v1
task_id: <task-id>
round: 1
responder: codex
created_at: 2026-05-14T12:34:56Z
accepted_findings:
rejected_findings:
fixed_findings:
requires_rereview: true
---
```

Body:

```markdown
# Codex Response

## Summary

Short summary of how Codex handled the review.

## Accepted Findings

List finding IDs and fixes.

## Rejected Findings

List finding IDs and reasons.

## Changes Made

Files changed and validation run.

## Re-review Request

Say whether another Claude round is needed and why.
```

After writing a Codex response:

- If re-review is needed, Codex increments `round`, updates `updated_at`, sets `status: ready_for_claude`, and updates `base_ref` / `head_ref` / `diff.patch` as needed.
- If consensus is reached, Codex sets `status: consensus_reached`.

## Review Timing

Use design review before implementation when the approach itself is uncertain.

Use code review after implementation when Claude should inspect a diff, commit, or patch.

Use re-review when Codex has responded to Claude findings and wants Claude to check the new round.

For risky work, the preferred sequence is:

```text
design_review -> code_review -> consensus_reached -> publish if requested/allowed
```

## D2R Modding Review Priorities

Claude should focus on:

- Does the change match Eric's original gameplay request?
- Are TSV column counts valid?
- Are empty TSV columns and trailing tabs preserved?
- Are active and base files synchronized when appropriate?
- Are tooltip strings consistent with actual gameplay fields?
- Are skill, missile, item, cube, and treasure-class mechanics likely valid?
- Could the change crash startup?
- Could the change silently do nothing because the wrong field was edited?
- Could existing items need respawn/cube refresh to show new stats?
- Were docs updated when new modding knowledge was learned?

## Publishing Rule

Claude never publishes.

Codex publishes only when Eric asks or when the current workflow explicitly allows automatic publish. Documentation-only changes do not need live publish.

Publish script:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install-local.ps1
```

After publishing data changes, Codex should verify live files when practical, for example with `Get-FileHash`.

## Git Rule

Eric wants every set of changes version controlled on GitHub.

Codex should commit and push completed changes unless Eric asks not to.

Claude does not commit or push.

## Subagent Rule

When Codex launches subagents:

- Tell them this protocol exists.
- Under the CLI mechanism, give them the reviewer session name/id when relevant: `d2r-codex-reviewer` / `da1ceeba-3d9c-44b1-a65f-fbcd0eb0950e`.
- Give them the legacy queue task ID only if one exists.
- Tell them not to edit review files outside their assigned task.
- Tell them not to publish or push unless explicitly assigned.
- Tell them not to bypass Claude review for risky changes.

If a subagent creates a patch for risky work, the parent Codex agent is responsible for creating or updating the Claude review task.
